Emma — quick update and delivery. Attached are the populated TIA scope and the bridge-letter draft. Below are the concise fallback bullets your legal team asked for; feel free to paste into your memo.

Fallback behavior (EU -> US routing):
- Routing decision: requests are routed by policy (region, capacity). When EU capacity is saturated, requests are routed to a compatible model variant in the nearest available region (US) with an automated notice to the customer via routing metadata.
- Data in-flight: payloads are TLS encrypted in transit; tokens are never stored in persistent customer-visible object stores when routed to US instances (ephemeral KV only).
- Logs and PII handling: operational logs for routing are pseudonymized; request/response content is redacted in sample logs — only request metadata (timestamp, region, model variant, token count) is visible in the sample bundle. Full request/response artifacts are available only under a joint-evidence NDA and legal request.
- Redress and rollback: automated rollback to queued onshore processing occurs when EU capacity returns; we can also enable size-limited onshore buffering for high-sensitivity tenants as a configuration.

UK IDTA stance: Redwood is willing to sign the standard UK IDTA addendum; we typically accept it with a short execution lead time for legal review. For MedicoRE we do not expect substantive redlines, but if you have a specific clause flagged we can escalate for a tracker review.
